summary.name: Tameo
summary.one_liner: Tameo is a free, open-source (MIT) macOS clipboard manager for Apple Silicon that keeps all copy history on the device, encrypted, and supports full-text and on-device OCR search.
use_cases: Recalling previously copied text or images on a Mac
Searching clipboard history by keyword, including text inside screenshots
Pasting frequently used snippets or templates
Keeping copied sensitive data out of stored history
Migrating from Clipy to a native Apple Silicon app
summary.what_it_does: Tameo runs in the menu bar and records everything copied, which can be recalled with a hotkey (⌘⇧V) in a palette and pasted into the current app by pressing number keys. It supports text, rich text, PDF, images, file paths, URLs and color codes. Search is incremental and normalizes Japanese full-width/half-width and kana variants, and on-device OCR makes text inside images searchable. Items can be pinned, filtered by type, previewed, and pasted as plain text (⌥) or transformed (⌃, e.g. full-width to half-width, removing URL tracking parameters). History is stored locally with AES-GCM encryption, with the key kept in the macOS Keychain.
notable: Fully local: no server, accounts, analytics or telemetry, and no external SDKs
On-device OCR search of text inside copied images and screenshots
Skips items marked as concealed by password managers, and reads clipboard contents only when the user selects an item to avoid macOS read notifications
Japanese JIS/kana input support and signed and notarized by ATI's Apple Developer ID
caveats: The app UI is in English only
Users on v0.1.10 or earlier must manually download the latest version because auto-update does not apply to them
